newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada eyes Asia, Latin America in financial talks.
newsitem.headline: Canada eyes Asia, Latin America in financial talks.

text.p: Canada, the World Trade Organisation's fourth top trading power, hopes this week's talks in Geneva to liberalise trade in financial services will improve access to markets in Asia and Latin America.

"We're looking for ... an agreement which will provide greater market access to countries and regions of interest to Canada," Sanjeev Chowdhury, spokesman for Canada's Trade Department, said in a telephone interview on Monday.
"Those regions which will be priorities to us in these negotiations will be Latin America and Asia Pacific," he said.
Canada proposed on Monday to open up its financial services market to suppliers from any WTO country and treat all suppliers the same way, senior Finance Department officials said.
"It's offering to give on a most-favoured-nation basis all that we've offered to any WTO (country) before, for all time," said one official who asked not to be identified.
Canada also offered to scrap any bilateral conditional agreements in financial services, officials said.

Canada's offer, however, did not include branching privileges for foreign banks -- the element for which most European financial institutions were watching -- officials said. The Finance Department has promised to change domestic legislation to give foreign banks more leeway to set up branches in Canada by the end of the year.
Canada's offer was conditional on other countries, especially emerging economies, beefing up their own offers, officials said.
"I guess it's not a secret there are countries in particular that we are aiming at," he said. "Asia and Latin America, those are areas (where) we'd like to see improvements."
Canada's offer would not require any changes to domestic legislation dealing with banks, securities and insurance.

Canada, the United States, the European Union and Japan have made it clear that reaching a successful financial services pact in time for the WTO deadline of December depended on generous offers this week from Asia and Latin America.

Japan offered last week to lift all restraints on foreign companies operating in its financial services sector. The European Union has said its new offer went beyond existing commitments, lifting 12 current restrictions and limiting other curbs.

The United States on Monday held out the offer of equal access to its market for all other countries in the WTO. But it said that key emerging economies would need to present significant liberalisation measures to make a deal possible.
Washington pulled out of the last bid to reach a global financial services pact in 1995, arguing that proposals from emerging economies were insufficient to justify opening the rich U.S. market.

Canadian government officials said they were confident that key countries would make improved offers this week in Geneva. But without U.S. support, the trade agreement would likely make little progress, participants in the negotiations said.
